senses.gloss:
इङ्ग् इङ्ग्, cl. 1. P., ep. A. इङ्गति, -ते,
इङ्गाञ्-चकार, इङ्गिष्यति, इङ्गितुम्, to
go, go to or towards; to move or agitate: Caus.
P. इङ्गयति, -यितुम्, to move, agitate, shake; (in
gram.) to divide or separate the members of a com-
pound word, to use a word or bring it into such a
grammatical relation that it is considered इङ्ग्य; see
below; [cf. Hib. ing, ‘a stir, a move.’]

इङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, movable, locomotive; surprising,
wonderful; (अस्), m. a hint or sign, an indication of
sentiment by gesture, knowledge; (आ), f. a kind of
counting.

इङ्गन, अम्, n. shaking; (in gram.) the operation
by which one member of a compound is separated
from another, as by the अव-ग्रह or mark of tmesis.

इङ्गित, अम्, n. palpitation, change of the voice,
internal motion, motion of various parts of the body
as indicating the intentions; hint, sign, gesture;
aim, intention, real but covert purpose.
—इङ्गित-
कोविद or इङ्गित-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, understanding
signs, acquainted with the gesture of another, skilled
in the expression or interpretation of the internal
sentiments by the external gesture.

इङ्ग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, movable from its place; in the
Prātiśākhyas a term for those words or rather parts
of a compound word which in certain grammatical
[]
operations may be separated from the preceding parts,
a word which in the Pada-pātḥa is divided by the
अव-ग्रह or mark of tmesis.
इङ्गिड इङ्गिड, N. of a plant, = इङ्गुद (?).

इङ्गुद इङ्गुद, अस्, ई, m. f., N. of a medicinal
tree, Terminalia Catappa; in Bengal confounded with
Putrañjīva Roxburghii Wall.; (अम्), n. the nut of
the tree Terminalia Catappa.

इङ्गुल, अस्, ई, m. f., N. of the tree Terminalia
Catappa.
